title: How to Add the Right Keywords to Your Resume to Beat ATS (with AI)
description:
----------------------------
Teal's Job Matcher shows you exactly how your resume stacks up against a job — and helps you add the right keywords to beat ATS. Watch how to find the keywords you're missing, add them with AI, and raise your match score in seconds.

If your resume isn't getting interviews, missing keywords are usually the reason. Job Matcher surfaces the exact hard and soft skills from any job description, scores your match, and shows you how to close the gap — without keyword stuffing.

transcript: [music] >> Teal's job matcher shows you exactly how your resume stacks up against the job you're targeting and tells you what to fix. >> [music] >> To get started, you'll need a resume in Teal. Then head to the job matcher tab in the top toolbar. From here, you can search jobs you've already saved, browse suggestions based on your target title and resume content, or search for job titles directly. Searching pulls from Teal's job board, millions of live listings. Click any job to review the description. When you find one that fits, click [music] match job. Teal surfaces the hard skills and soft skills from that job description and calculates your match score. Your match score reflects how many of the job's keywords appear in your resume. Add more keywords and your score goes up. >> [music] >> The keyword list shows what's already in your resume and what's missing. >> [music] >> You can view keywords on their own or toggle to see them in context against the full job summary. For any missing keyword, you have four options. Write a bullet, add to skills, scroll to it in the job description, or ignore it. Let's write a bullet. Select a position, choose your keyword, in this case case management, and click generate bullet. Teal generates several options that use the keyword in context. Adjust any metrics to match your actual experience, then save. Watch your match score update. You can also add keywords directly to your skills section. If you have experience with a skill and it fits there naturally, add it. That said, Teal recommends placing keywords in your experience bullets whenever possible. >> [music] >> Keywords in context carry more weight. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
